doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Carnival versus medicine shows, gilly shows and minstrels
summary: Distinguishing carnivals from medicine shows and minstrels; the jig show at the back of the midway.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: No, no. This had nothing to do – minstrels were like Silas Green from New Orleans, all those things. This was strictly carnival. Carnival was . . .
Rides, yeah. Games. Right. Trinkets and gadgets, yeah.
How did that differ from a medicine show?
A medicine show was just a little truck show that went from one area to the other. The cat selling something that you could drink or something that you could put in. . .
So that the medicine show experience is like the one that [ ? ? ] the monkeys. That was more like a medicine show.

No, that was a small – it was sort of like a medicine show, but it was a gilly show, we called it. A small truck carnival, where they – see, our show was a [?] show. This was a truck show. They had – it was a smaller thing. It was operated in – they operated in smaller towns and a smaller number of things on the carnival, fewer rides and fewer things, but they – for the most part they had what they referred to in those days as a jig show, which they were derogatorily referring to us in. Our shows would always – on the big shows, the back – the end of the midway – the midway – the carnival was set up, you walk in, go along this avenue and then around the end and you come back out the other avenue. That was the routine. In between were all sorts of shops and games and things to try out. On the outside was the same thing, all the way down, around. Our show was always the last one in the back.

Not – we were doing the same type of show that you would see in a lot of clubs today: the comedian, the shake dancer, the chorus girls, the production numbers, and the band played. An emcee and all that. The same . . .
It was sort of like a floor show [ ? ? ].
